title: Per-row lemma dispatch for FKS2 Corollary 24's eleven Table-7 rows
intent: Assemble FKS2's Corollary 24 — the pointwise bound Eπ x ≤ B x for every row (B, I) of the eleven-row Table 7 — from one named lemma per row: the glue proves (B, I) ∈ table7 by an eleven-way case split and hands each row to its own corollary_24_row1 … row11, each declared and proved in its own file, leaving the glue at 18 lines.

parent.name: corollary_24_all
parent.statement:
theorem corollary_24_all (B : ℝ → ℝ) (I : Set ℝ) (h : (B, I) ∈ table7) :
    ∀ x, Real.log x ∈ I → Eπ x ≤ B x

applicability.goal_shape: A target theorem `corollary_24_all (B : ℝ → ℝ) (I : Set ℝ) (h : (B, I) ∈ table7) : ∀ x, Real.log x ∈ I → Eπ x ≤ B x` whose only substantive hypothesis is a finite list-membership `(B, I) ∈ table7` — a disjunction over eleven explicit pairs — so the proof is a case split, one case per row.
applicability.use_when: The cases are a finite, explicit table and each case is substantial enough to deserve its own declaration and file; the shared machinery is factored into one template file that the other cases instantiate (here FKS2Cor24Row11 carries the generic x^{-1/n} helpers that rows 6–11 clone at n = 3, 4, 5, 10, 50, 100).
applicability.avoid_when: The cases differ only in a scalar or a numeric bound, in which case one parameterised lemma beats a family of clones; or the case set is open-ended rather than a finite list membership, so there is no exhaustive case split to dispatch.

claims.claim: `PrimeNumberTheoremAnd/IEANTN/FKS2Cor24All.lean` contains no `sorry`, `admit`, or `axiom` token in lines 1–50.

The glue `corollary_24_all` is 18 lines and dispatches 11 direct per-row lemmas; the longest chain of project-lemma citations below the parent is depth 5 (corollary_24_all → corollary_24_row4 → floor_row4 → floor_xhalf_of_check → Epi_le_evalLhsE_wide → Buthe.theorem_2e); the eight shown children have 29, 30, 30, 29, 29, 32, 32 and 32 lines.

metrics.how_counted: 8 of the 11 direct row lemmas are child sites; rows 7, 8, 9 are listed in README.md with permalinks because they are clones of row 6 (n = 4, 5, 10 respectively)

consequences: Creates one named child lemma per table row (here eleven), so the glue is a mechanical case split over `table7` whose exhaustiveness and injectivity (`Prod.mk.injEq`) are discharged by `simp` and the eleven-way `rcases`; the final `| h` branch closes by `absurd h (by simp)` because a list-membership disjunction of eleven explicit pairs is exhaustive. Each row lemma then carries its own per-segment decomposition (a trichotomy on x plus a two- or three-segment dispatch), so the row lemmas are the real content and the glue stays 18 lines. Failure modes: a row whose proof does not factor into the shared template is still forced into its own file, so each per-row file must be genuinely self-contained; if two rows shared one argument they would duplicate it unless the shared machinery is lifted (as rows 1–5 lift the x^{-1/2} floor machinery and rows 6–11 the x^{-1/n} machinery into Table4Ext). Trust boundary: the row lemmas close without `sorry`, and their Buthe-floor and mid-envelope segments are proved by the dyadic interval kernel (`native_decide`); their floor-trusted, band and sliver segments delegate to `FKS2.Cor24Trusted.*` (and rows 1/10/11's floor-checked to `FKS2.Cor24Checked.*`), which are the project's authorised trusted (`sorry`-closed) Theorem-6 interpolation results.
